title: Summer Rade vs Vigil of Masis
lede:
The Summer Rade beat the Vigil of Masis 43-19 on Victory Points in Battle Round 6, sitting on 29 after Round 5 and scoring 14 in the last round.

The Rade's mobile Sidhe units outshot and outfought the Vigil everywhere but the centre, destroying seven units for two and completing four secondaries, while the Vigil scored objectives only in Rounds 2 and 4, when the Rade's units stepped off the centre after their own attacks.
result_line: Summer Rade win 43-19 on Victory Points in Battle Round 6
deployment:
Central Faceoff on CROSSROADS, three objectives on row 7: the 3 VP centre at (7,7) and 2 VP flanks at (1,7) and (13,7). The Summer Rade spread along row 12 in front of its HQ at (7,13): Sidhe Wardens 3 with the Sidhe Druid at (3,12), the Wild Hunt Riders at (4,12) and the Moonless Veilblades at (5,12) on the left; the Redcap Reivers at (8,12), Sidhe Wardens 1 with High King Finvarra at (9,12), Sidhe Wardens 2 at (10,12) and the Blackflint Archers at (11,12) on the right. The Vigil of Masis set up along rows 1 and 2 in front of its HQ at (7,1): Azat Lancers 2 at (3,1) and Pahak Riflemen 3 at (4,2) on the left, Pahak Riflemen 2 with the Dream-Reader of Tir at (5,2), the Vishap Harpooners with the Reedfire Champion at (7,2), Pahak Riflemen 1 with Andranik Ozanian at (9,2), Azat Lancers 1 at (11,1) and the Parsawor Grenadiers at (11,2). The Rade had Priority with fewer units on the battlefield (10 to 11).

Both armies set up wide. The Rade's units are fast and fragile (5-HP Warden squads with EVASION and Fading Step, 3-HP Veilblades); the Vigil's are ten-model rifle squads, two 20-HP lancer squads and a slow grenade team. The Rade could reach all three objectives in one move; the Vigil could not.

1.title: The Rade take all three objectives

feed.text: Primaries revealed: BLEED THEM WHITE for the Rade, IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS for the Vigil. Secondaries kept: FORWARD PRESENCE and PUSH FORWARD. Archfey of Knock Ma let the Rade roll two dice for the Flow of Magic and keep Tree. Vahagn's Quarry named the Wild Hunt Riders. The Rade spent its 2 CP on Double Time for Sidhe Wardens 1, a move the record says was in reach anyway.

Sidhe Wardens 1 and High King Finvarra advanced to 6,6 and Sidhe Wardens 3 with the Druid to 6,8, both in the centre's area. The Wild Hunt Riders reached 0,8 on the left objective; Sidhe Wardens 2 and the Archers 12,7 and 12,8 on the right. The Vigil pushed Pahak Riflemen 1 and Andranik Ozanian to 8,7, on the centre, with the Azat Lancers at 9,6 and 4,7 and Pahak Riflemen 2 at 8,5.

Andranik gave Pahak Riflemen 1 a Go to Ground (1 CP), and the Blackflint Archers still put 6 into them (20 to 14, three Pahak). The Reedfire Champion's Name the Quarry moved the QUARRY to Sidhe Wardens 3. Every other unit had no legal action.
The Rade scored all three: the centre on OC 26 vs 17, the left (OC 5 vs 0) and the right (OC 15 vs 0), 7 VP. 7-0.

2.title: Pahak Riflemen 1 shot away, but Azat Lancers 1 takes the centre

feed.text: The Flow of Magic gave Surge. The Vigil put Double Time on Pahak Riflemen 3 (3 CP); the Rade spent nothing. Secondaries kept: TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY and IRON GRIP.

The Redcap Reivers charged the Parsawor Grenadiers at 11,5 and the Moonless Veilblades charged Azat Lancers 2 at 3,7 behind Finvarra's 1 CP Go to Ground; both targets fell back, to 9,5 and 5,9. Azat Lancers 1 charged Finvarra, Sidhe Wardens 1, Sidhe Wardens 3 and the Druid at 7,7, and Sidhe Wardens 3 fell back to 10,9. Pahak Riflemen 1 stepped to 8,6 under a second Go to Ground (1 CP) and lost 4 to Overwatch from Sidhe Wardens 2 and 3 and the Wild Hunt Riders. Pahak Riflemen 3 ran 1,5 to 6,4 on its Double Time, away from the left objective it had been heading for.

The Archers put 6 more into Pahak Riflemen 1 (10 to 4). Azat Lancers 1 did 2 to Sidhe Wardens 1 (5 to 3); Finvarra's Mayfire Scepter answered with 3 and BURNED, Sidhe Wardens 1 with 1 (20 to 16). Sidhe Wardens 1's Fading Step then took it and Finvarra to 4,5, out of the centre. The Wild Hunt Riders took 1 off Pahak Riflemen 1 and Sidhe Wardens 2 finished them (3, and 1 on Andranik): Pahak Riflemen 1 destroyed. Andranik's Second Watch put VIGIL on the Archers. The Dream-Reader channelled 4 Mana and the Druid 6. BURNED took 2 off Azat Lancers 1 (14).

The Vigil took the centre on OC 11 vs 0 (3 VP) and IRON GRIP (+2 VP, +1 CP) for Azat Lancers 1's 7+ OC there; the Rade kept the left (2) but nobody stayed on the right. BLEED THEM WHITE paid the Rade 2 (one kill, no loss), IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS the Vigil 3. 11-8.

3.title: The fresh Pahak Riflemen die the round they arrive

feed.text: The Vigil spent 7 of its 8 CP: Double Time on Pahak Riflemen 3 again (2) and Troop Requisition (5), a new Pahak Riflemen at 6,2. Secondaries kept: OBJECTIVE RELAY and FOCUSED FIRE; PUSH FORWARD expired.

The Vigil had Priority. Andranik walked off the centre to 8,3, and when Sidhe Wardens 2 charged Azat Lancers 1 at 8,8 the Lancers fell back to 5,9: the centre emptied. Azat Lancers 2 rode to 0,8 on the left objective and the Moonless Veilblades charged them at 1,8; Sidhe Wardens 1 and Finvarra stepped onto the left at 2,6. The Redcap Reivers charged the Parsawor Grenadiers again (10,6) and the Grenadiers fell back again (8,5). The new Pahak Riflemen went to 3,2.

Pahak Riflemen 2 shot Sidhe Wardens 2 for 4 (5 to 1). The Veilblades put 12 into Azat Lancers 2 (20 to 8). The Archers took the Grenadiers to 1 HP (5). The Wild Hunt Riders (9), Sidhe Wardens 3 (6) and Sidhe Wardens 1 (5) shot the requisitioned Pahak Riflemen: destroyed, 5 CP gone in one Action Phase. Finvarra cast Feth Fiada on the Veilblades for 1 Mana under Surge. BURNED took 2 more off Azat Lancers 1 (12).
Only the left was held, by the Rade on OC 11 vs 4: 2 VP, and TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY (+3) for one objective to none. BLEED THEM WHITE 2. IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 2. 18-10.

4.title: The Veilblades finish Azat Lancers 2; the centre slips away again

feed.text: The Rade's Troop Requisition (5 CP) placed a new Sidhe Wardens at 7,12. The Vigil put Double Time on Pahak Riflemen 3 a third time (2 CP) and a Rally Cry on the Parsawor Grenadiers (2 CP). Sidhe Wardens 2 failed Morale and was SUPPRESSED. Secondaries kept: VIGILANT WATCH and INTO THE FRAY; FOCUSED FIRE expired.

The Wild Hunt Riders moved from 4,5 to 7,8, on the centre, completing OBJECTIVE RELAY (+2 VP, +1 CP); the Archers came to 6,8 beside them. The Redcap Reivers took the right objective at 12,6 and the Veilblades charged Azat Lancers 2 again. Pahak Riflemen 2 with the Dream-Reader and the Grenadiers stepped into the centre's area at 7,6 and 8,6; Pahak Riflemen 3 went 5,3 to 1,4 and hit Sidhe Wardens 1 with Overwatch as it came to 2,7.

The Veilblades did 8: Azat Lancers 2 destroyed. The Dream-Reader's 4 Mana Reedfire was countered by the Druid's Gaeth Druad for 4 Mana. The Archers put 9 into Pahak Riflemen 2 (20 to 11); the Grenadiers, rerolling through VIGIL, bombed them for 2 (5 to 3) and the Archers' Fading Step took them to 4,7. The Wild Hunt Riders (4), Sidhe Wardens 3 (4) and Sidhe Wardens 2 (2) took Pahak Riflemen 2 down to 1 HP, and the Riders' Fading Step took them to 7,10. Pahak Riflemen 3 shot Sidhe Wardens 1 off the table (2, and 1 on Finvarra): Sidhe Wardens 1 destroyed, Finvarra stepping away to 1,9.

The Fading Steps left no Rade unit on the centre, and the Vigil scored it on OC 3 vs 0 with one rifleman, the Dream-Reader and the Grenadiers. The Rade held the left (OC 3) and the right (OC 5), 4 VP. BLEED THEM WHITE paid nothing (one kill for one loss). IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 2. 24-15.

5.title: A grenade kills Pahak Riflemen 2; the Rade stop one short

feed.text: The Vigil's second Troop Requisition (5 CP) placed Pahak Riflemen at 8,2; the Rade put Double Time on Finvarra (2 CP). The Flow of Magic gave Earth. Secondaries kept: COORDINATED PUSH and SECURE THE FLANKS; FORWARD PRESENCE expired.

Azat Lancers 1 charged the Blackflint Archers from 2,11 to 3,6, completing INTO THE FRAY (+2); the Archers failed their Fall Back test, losing a model, and ended at 4,10. The Wild Hunt Riders charged the Dream-Reader and Pahak Riflemen 2 from 6,7, the Redcap Reivers the new Pahak Riflemen at 11,3, the Veilblades Pahak Riflemen 3 at 0,7. Finvarra, the new Sidhe Wardens and Sidhe Wardens 2 and 3 closed on the centre, and COORDINATED PUSH completed (+2 VP, +1 CP).

The Parsawor Grenadiers bombed 6,8: 1 each on the new Sidhe Wardens and Sidhe Wardens 3, and Sidhe Wardens 2 destroyed; the same blast hit the Dream-Reader's squad and destroyed Pahak Riflemen 2, the Vigil's own unit. The Veilblades put 15 into Pahak Riflemen 3 (20 to 5). The Dream-Reader attacked the Wild Hunt Riders, who struck first: Dream-Reader of Tir destroyed, and the Grenadiers failed Morale. The Redcap Reivers' Dual Wield put 16 into the new Pahak Riflemen (20 to 4). The two Warden squads shot Azat Lancers 1 for 4 (12 to 8). Finvarra channelled 6 Mana and the Druid spent 2 on Feth Fiada for the Riders.

The Wild Hunt Riders held the centre alone (OC 5 vs 0), 3 VP; the left tied 3-3 between the Veilblades and Pahak Riflemen 3. BLEED THEM WHITE paid nothing: the Dream-Reader for Sidhe Wardens 2, and Pahak Riflemen 2's death was not the Rade's. IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS 1. 29-18, one short of the target.

6.title: Fourteen VP in the last round

feed.text: The Rade kept OMNIPRESENCE and put Secure Objective on the Moonless Veilblades (3 CP); the Vigil put Double Time on Andranik (2 CP) and kept PROBING STRIKE. VIGILANT WATCH expired. The Grenadiers failed Morale again.

Andranik ran 9,4 to 8,8, into the centre. The new Sidhe Wardens charged Azat Lancers 1 and Pahak Riflemen 3 at 2,7 and the Veilblades charged Azat Lancers 1 at 1,6; Pahak Riflemen 3 fell back to 1,3, the new Pahak Riflemen from the Redcap Reivers to 13,2. The Reivers went back to the right objective at 12,6, Finvarra to 6,8 on the centre and the Archers to 6,9; the Vigil's two Overwatch shots both missed.

The Veilblades put 7 into Azat Lancers 1 (8 to 1) and the new Sidhe Wardens finished them: Azat Lancers 1 destroyed. The Vishap Harpooners, rerolling through VIGIL, hit the Wild Hunt Riders for 4 and the Grenadiers' bomb for 2 more (10 to 4). The Riders answered: Parsawor Grenadiers destroyed. The Archers (3) and Sidhe Wardens 3 (1) took Andranik to 2 HP; Finvarra's Mayfire missed.

The Rade scored all three objectives (centre OC 7 vs 3, left OC 14 vs 0, right OC 5 vs 0), 7 VP, BLEED THEM WHITE 3 for two kills without a loss, and OMNIPRESENCE (+4). IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS gave the Vigil 1. 43-19, Summer Rade win.

analysis.title: Why it went this way
analysis.html:
Where the VP came from

The Summer Rade scored 25 objective VP (7 in Round 1 and 7 in Round 6, 11 in between), 7 from BLEED THEM WHITE and 11 from four secondaries: TERRITORIAL SUPERIORITY 3, OBJECTIVE RELAY 2, COORDINATED PUSH 2 and OMNIPRESENCE 4. The Vigil of Masis scored 6 objective VP, the centre in Rounds 2 and 4, 9 from IMPENETRABLE FORTRESS and 4 from IRON GRIP and INTO THE FRAY. The Rade completed four of its six secondaries; the Vigil two of six.

{{chart:objectives}}

What the key units did

The Wild Hunt Riders (25 RP) were the Rade's best unit: 11.2 VP with 7 hinged on them, 44.9 per 100 RP, the left objective in Rounds 1 and 2, OBJECTIVE RELAY, the centre alone in Round 5, and 21 damage with two kills (the Dream-Reader and the Grenadiers). The Moonless Veilblades did 42 damage, more than the whole Vigil army's 22: 20 to destroy Azat Lancers 2 over two rounds, 15 into Pahak Riflemen 3 and 7 into Azat Lancers 1, without losing a model. The Blackflint Archers added 29, most of it into Pahak Riflemen 1 and 2. The Redcap Reivers held the right objective in Rounds 4 and 6 (6.4 VP, 4 hinged) and twice drove the Grenadiers back. High King Finvarra (70 RP) did 3 damage and scored 6.2 VP standing on objectives.

For the Vigil, Azat Lancers 1 did the scoring (6.7 VP: the centre and IRON GRIP in Round 2, INTO THE FRAY in Round 5) and did 2 damage. The Parsawor Grenadiers did 8, one of them to their own Pahak Riflemen 2. Over the battle the Rade dealt 146 damage to 22 and seven Vigil units died (148 RP, one of them the Vigil's own kill) for two of the Rade's (34 RP).

{{chart:attrition}}

What the Vigil could not do

  • Hold the centre. It took the centre twice, both times after the Rade had stepped off it, and lost it both times the next round: Azat Lancers 1 fell back from Sidhe Wardens 2's charge in Round 3, and the Rade's Wild Hunt Riders took it back in Round 5.
  • Reach the flanks. Pahak Riflemen 3 had three Double Times (7 CP) and wandered 1,5 to 6,4 to 5,3 to 1,4 to 1,6; its only objective result was the 3-3 tie on the left in Round 5. Azat Lancers 2 reached the left in Round 3 and was cut down by the Veilblades.
  • Its secondaries: PUSH FORWARD needed two Advances ending in the enemy half in one phase; FOCUSED FIRE three units on one target in one Action Phase; SECURE THE FLANKS a unit in the enemy half near a side edge, and PROBING STRIKE attacks on three units in that half, in the last two rounds, when the Vigil was falling back.
  • Make its command points count. It spent 10 CP on two Troop Requisitions: the first Pahak Riflemen were destroyed in the round they arrived, the second were cut to 4 HP by the Redcap Reivers and fell back to the corner.

The Rade's two failed secondaries: FORWARD PRESENCE (a unit within 3 squares of the Vigil's HQ, which nothing went near) and VIGILANT WATCH (an Overwatch from an Objective Area; the Rade fired no Overwatch in Rounds 4 to 6).

{{chart:rp-trade}}

The AI, not the army

  • Fading Step off the centre. After attacking, the Rade's units used Fading Step to step away, and the squares the AI chose cost it the centre twice. In Round 2 Sidhe Wardens 3 had already fallen back from Azat Lancers 1, and Sidhe Wardens 1's Fading Step took Finvarra from 6,6 to 4,5: the Vigil scored the centre's 3 VP and IRON GRIP's 2. In Round 4 the Wild Hunt Riders (7,8 to 7,10) and the Archers (6,8 to 4,7) stepped off it and the Vigil scored it on OC 3 vs 0. Those 3 VP were the margin between finishing in Round 5 and finishing in Round 6.
  • Round 5, the Parsawor Grenadiers' bomb on 6,8 destroyed the Vigil's own Pahak Riflemen 2, which stood at 7,6, two squares from the target square of an AOE 1 weapon. The Wild Hunt Riders at 6,7, inside the blast and engaged with that squad, took no hit: the splash on them looks to have been passed to the unit they were fighting by the shooting-into-melee rule. That is a rules question rather than the army, and the record also credits the Grenadiers with Pahak Riflemen 2 as a kill.
  • Pahak Riflemen 3 and the Double Times above: 7 CP to move a rifle squad back and forth on the left. The Vigil gained 24 CP and spent 23 to the Rade's 13, most of it on those Double Times and the two Troop Requisitions, and none of it decided an objective.
  • The Reedfire Champion and the Vishap Harpooners (47 RP) were idle in five of six rounds behind the Vigil's lines; their only actions were Name the Quarry in Round 1 and the Harpooners' shot at the Wild Hunt Riders in Round 6.
  • Round 4, Reedfire: the Dream-Reader's 4 Mana spell was countered by the Druid's Gaeth Druad, which cost the Rade 4 Mana too. Feth Fiada (four casts, 6 Mana) bought nothing the record can price.
  • The Fall Back record is inflated by the AI's charge-planning probes: six of its ten 'stayed' entries (Azat Lancers 1, Sidhe Wardens 2 and the Archers in Round 2, the Vishap Harpooners in Round 3, Sidhe Wardens 2 and the Veilblades in Round 5) name an engager that was never adjacent.

The result is mostly the army: the Rade's Veilblades and archers out-damaged everything the Vigil had, and its speed put a unit on every objective in Rounds 1 and 6. The AI made it closer than it was by stepping off the centre twice, and the Vigil's AI spent its larger CP income on moves and reinforcements that scored nothing.

closing: The Summer Rade took all three objectives in Round 1 and all three again in Round 6; between them the Veilblades, the Archers and the Wild Hunt Riders shot and cut down seven Vigil units. The Vigil's only objective VP came from ground the Rade's Fading Steps gave up.
